patterns.usage_note: Voices a wish the speaker cannot count on: a whole clause plus と＋いい／よい／ありがたい in dictionary form, closed with がな(あ), reads as "I do hope …" with a hint that it may not come off (雨がやむとよいがなあ). A sibling entry is the western-dialect protest particle, irritated that the hearer missed the obvious (それくらいできるがな, さっき言うたがな). The drawn-out がなあ is the usual shape, and it suits relaxed, somewhat older-sounding speech.

examples.ruby: 息子[むすこ]の就職[しゅうしょく]がうまく決[き]まるといいがな。
examples.english: I do hope my son's job hunt works out.

examples.ruby: 出[で]かけるまでに雨[あめ]がやんでくれるとよいがな。
examples.english: It'd be nice if the rain let up before we head out.

examples.ruby: 孫[まご]が正月[しょうがつ]に顔[かお]を見[み]せてくれるとありがたいがな。
examples.english: It'd mean a lot if the grandkids showed up at New Year's.
